policy_upcoming.what_happened: Temporary regulations were issued concerning a new nonrefundable Federal tax credit for qualified contributions to scholarship granting organizations.
policy_upcoming.effect: A new nonrefundable Federal tax credit becomes available for qualified contributions to scholarship granting organizations in 2027 and later taxable years.

policy_upcoming.what_happened: Final rules set forth requirements for price transparency reporting for non-grandfathered group health plans and health insurance issuers.
policy_upcoming.effect: Your employer health insurance plan has new price transparency reporting requirements that become effective on December 7, 2026.

policy_upcoming.what_happened: A Utah bill modifies provisions related to the property tax exemption process.
policy_upcoming.effect: Once you own a home, you will have deadlines for filing an application for a property tax exemption with the county board of equalization and for the board to render a decision.

policy_upcoming.what_happened: A bill amends requirements for health insurance preauthorization in Utah.
policy_upcoming.effect: Your health insurer must make an authorization or adverse preauthorization determination within a defined maximum time.

policy_upcoming.what_happened: Final regulations provide guidance for automatic enrollment requirements that apply to certain retirement plans.
policy_upcoming.effect: Your retirement plan participation is subject to new automatic enrollment requirements starting January 19, 2027.

policy_calendar.label: FHFA conforming loan limit for next year — expected late November
policy_calendar.note: The cap on a conforming (non-jumbo) mortgage, and the line between a normal rate and a jumbo one. FHFA has announced it in the last days of November each year, and the new limit applies to loans made from January 1.

tech.summary: Quantum computing firms are exploring practical applications in the energy sector, including optimizing energy grids, developing solar materials, and creating hydrogen catalysts, potentially leading to its first real-world payoff in energy rather than drug discovery.

United Nations diplomats failed to agree on regulations for autonomous weapons, often referred to as 'killer robots,' after a week of negotiations in Geneva, instead agreeing only to begin discussing options.
Developers are working on AI-assisted Rust servers for Python applications, such as 'Muru' by the creator of mod_WSGI, indicating advances in leveraging AI for server-side development.

world.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has urged the United States to supply Patriot missiles after a Russian drone attack near Kyiv killed at least two people, and shelling in Zaporizhzhia killed one.
Drone attacks near Sudan's capital, Khartoum, killed four people and reportedly damaged a UN building and the city's airport, with blame directed at the Rapid Support Forces.
Saudi Arabia intercepted a drone and missile, while Houthi media reported an attack on an oil company in Sanaa that injured several people, as regional tensions continue.

us.summary: A federal jury convicted 30-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht for starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles, which tragically killed 12 people.
Thanksgiving holiday travel is threatened by anticipated storms on both the East and West coasts, with San Francisco's mayor advising residents against non-essential travel.
A permitting reform bill passed in the Senate aims to accelerate the development of renewable energy projects.

science.summary: Scientists have successfully sequenced the entire genome of a whale by using commercial drones fitted with petri dishes to collect snot samples.
Early trials of a daily pill called daraxonrasib have shown promise in shrinking and potentially eliminating tumors in some patients with pancreatic cancer.

weekly_recap: This week began with SpaceX achieving a major milestone by successfully catching its Starship rocket with its 'Mechazilla' launch tower after orbit on November 15. The United States officially lost its measles elimination status, confirmed on November 17, amid a significant outbreak. Global financial markets experienced considerable turbulence, marked by a tech sell-off, including Nvidia's stock decline following a new Commerce Department rule targeting China's chip access and the resignation of its former CEO. Anthropic's IPO set a record on November 19, valued at $81.3 billion, but its public debut on November 20 contributed to a broader slump in global stock markets, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite entering correction territory. Geopolitically, major global leaders gathered in China for the APEC summit on November 18, and the UN's top court ruled on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority. In the US, the Senate passed bipartisan legislation on November 20 to accelerate permitting reviews for energy and data center infrastructure. The week concluded with international climate talks at COP31 in a deadlock over fossil fuels and UN discussions failing to yield binding rules for autonomous weapons on November 21.
